summary: IGNIS-SI is a Super-Intelligence (SI) powered web dashboard that summarizes, ranks, and interprets NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data—anchored on PSI-26 (Burning and Suppression of Solids - BASS)—to safeguard future human spaceflight on the Moon, Mars, and deep-space transit. While fire alarms like the recent Artemis II event highlight the urgency of spacecraft fire safety, raw PSI data across hundreds of test runs and technical presentations is complex to compare. IGNIS-SI transforms 115 validated ISS test runs and empirical flame-spread physics into an interactive Mission Control interface. Users can simulate habitable crew environments—including planned ≥30% O₂, ≤10.2 psi Lunar Bases and pressurized rovers—to instantly identify Upward Limiting Oxygen Index (ULOI) material failures, extract CFD modeling constants, enforce ventilation-coupled suppression rules, and explore terrestrial spin-offs such as fine-water-mist extinguishers and firefighter protective gear.
details:
IGNIS-SI is an interactive, six-tab Mission Control dashboard built around NASA PSI-26 (BASS) and benchmarked against companion PSI studies (BASS-II, ACME CFI-G, SAFFIRE-I, SAME, and ACME E-FIELD Flames).

  1. Autonomous Mission Risk & ULOI Ranker: Evaluates spacecraft materials (Ultem 1000, Nomex HT90-40, Nomex-III, SIBAL cotton-fiberglass, PMMA acrylic, and paraffin/Japan wax) against user-configured cabin oxygen (15%–40% O₂) and ventilation speeds (0–45 cm/s). It automatically triggers critical alerts when oxygen levels exceed material ULOI thresholds—demonstrating how polymers safe on the ISS (21–22% O₂) become flammable in ≥30% O₂, ≤10.2 psi Lunar habitats and pressurized rovers.
  2. Interactive PSI-26 Experimental Explorer: Parses and visualizes 115 valid ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) burns across 41 physical samples, detailing constant apparatus parameters (76×76 mm SPICE flow duct, 29-gage Kanthal igniter, and Nikon D300S 16-bit NEF imaging diagnostics) versus manipulated test variables.
  3. Cross-Investigation & Hardware Comparator: Side-by-side comparison matrix contrasting MSG-based solid combustion (BASS) with Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) gaseous/high-O₂ studies (ACME CFI-G up to 85% O₂), large-scale Cygnus tests (SAFFIRE-I), aerosol detection (SAME), and electric-field partial-gravity proxies (ACME E-FIELD Flames).
  4. Predictive Modeling & Physics Engine: Plots empirical concurrent vs. opposed flame spread equations ($V_F = 0.20\,U_\infty + 0.56\text{ mm/s}$ for 2 cm SIBAL) and exports machine-readable CFD boundary conditions (CSV) and downloadable Engineering Safety Briefs (Markdown).
  5. Next-Gen Controls & Earth Spin-Offs: Translates PSI-26 wake-flame suppression findings (where 500 cc/min Nitrogen jets fail without cutting airflow to 0 cm/s) into automated HVAC-suppression interlock rules, multi-spectral smoke/dust detectors, and terrestrial spin-offs for firefighter PPE and fine-water-mist extinguishers.
  6. Grounded SI Fire Safety Co-Pilot: An AI advisor backed by Google Gemini and deterministic physics rules that answers complex aerospace fire-safety queries with direct PSI-26 citations.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages & Data Processing: Python 3.12, Pandas, Regular Expressions, JSON/TSV data cleaning pipelines.
  • Frontend & Visualization: Streamlit, Plotly Express & Plotly Graph Objects.
  • Super-Intelligence (SI) & AI: Google Gemini API (gemini-2.5-flash) paired with a custom deterministic rule-based SI reasoning engine (si_engine.py).

Creativity & Design Considerations Rather than displaying static spreadsheets, we engineered IGNIS-SI around real mission constraints: the Partial-Gravity Bounding Gap (using 0g + 1g envelopes and electric-field proxies since true 1/6g Lunar and 3/8g Martian combustion data from LUCI/FM2 is not yet in PSI) and the Ventilation-Suppression Paradox (proving inert gas alone cannot extinguish shielded wake flames without shutting down cabin airflow).
